messages:
miriam: quick q — i'm drafting this week's oncall swap note. can we lock down who owns what for a latency spike or model quality regression? trying to avoid cross-pager noise.

alex: short version: runtime owns model-serving surface (model binaries, quantization, batching, KV cache, runtime config + rollbacks). SRE owns infra (nodes, networking, autoscaler, storage, kubernetes control plane).

alex: escalation heuristics i've been using: if it's model-behavior / logits / hallucination / output-quality -> runtime. If it's node OOM, disk pressure, cloud region outage, or control-plane errors -> eng-sre.

devon: + a practical pager flow proposal:
```
if p95_latency > 500ms for 5m => page runtime-oncall
if error_rate > 5% (user-facing 5xxs) => page runtime-oncall then eng-sre if persists > 10m
if node OOM / node notReady / kube-apiserver errors => page eng-sre immediately
if region-wide infra alerts (cloud provider) => page eng-sre and channel incident
```
(we can tweak thresholds, but good to codify)

oncall-bot: FYI miriam: your swap is scheduled for 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC. Reminder: add runbooks you expect the next oncall to check. :bell:

ravi: how are we defining "incident" vs "degradation" here? in past we've had ambiguity — e.g., 10% slowdown in embeddings but no dropped requests. do we treat that as incident?

alex: i recommend: incident = user-visible outage or SLA breach (latency or error rate beyond SLOs) OR cascading failures (multiple dependent subsystems). degradation = measurable drop in performance/quality that doesn't yet breach SLOs; treat as high-priority FYI. if degradation starts trending toward SLO breach, escalate to incident.

sam: can we add a small handoff checklist to the swap note? minimal items i want: active rollouts, recent canary metrics, open alerts, top-3 tickets, runbook links, and what to watch for in next 2 hours. sample template: 
- swap owner: @miriam (until 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC)
- active rollouts: model-v2.1 (canary 10%) -> link: https://confluence/redwood/model-rollouts
- watch: p95 gen latency, 5xx rate, kv-cache hitrate
- runbooks: /runbooks/runtime-latency, /runbooks/eng-sre-node-oom
- escalation: runtime-oncall -> eng-sre (after 10m) -> oncall-escalation (exec)

miriam: love that checklist. i'll add it. can someone own updating the severity definitions doc? i think language is messy right now.

alex: i'll take it. i'll add concrete examples (db fail vs model hallucination vs autoscaler misbehave) and sync to the runbooks. ping me if you want edits.

ravi: one more edge: private deployments / customer-dedicated pools — who handles customer network/link issues? typically eng-sre for infra, but runtime should own fallbacks (serve smaller model) when capacity constrained. call it out in the doc.

devon: agreed — add a line: for customer-dedicated/private: first check customer network and VPC (eng-sre), but runtime should try local fallbacks and circuit-breaker behaviour before paging customers.

miriam: thanks all. i'll update the swap thread with the checklist + links and tag runtime-oncall schedule. goal: leave a <3 minute read for next person. :heart:

sam: :thumbsup: will skim and add any missing tickets.

oncall-bot: note added to swap doc by miriam at 2026-04-01T18:48:40Z.

miriam: done — updated and linked the runbooks. if you see anything missing, reply here and i'll patch before handoff.
